surprises.description: The preview’s $112.70 million sales consensus was exceeded: Flexsteel reported $114.0 million, near the top of its $111–115 million guidance range. This was a modest beat rather than a result above the company’s guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 FY2027 net sales rose 3.2% year-over-year to $114.0 million, near the top of the 1%-4% guidance range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | Q1 FY27 Consensus | $112.70M”; company guidance was “$111–115M (+1% to +4%).”

surprises.description: Demand and volume in the continuing Flexsteel-branded business were stronger than the preview’s base case of roughly flat volume ex-Homestyles. Continuing branded sales and orders each grew about 5%, with backlog up 8.2%, and growth initiatives delivered meaningful unit gains.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Excluding the exited Home Styles ready-to-assemble category, continuing Flexsteel-branded sales grew approximately 5%, with orders up ~5% and ending backlog up 8.2% to $77.7 million”; “several growth initiatives also delivered meaningful unit volume gains.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “volume roughly flat ex-Homestyles”; its bull case expected unit volume up year over year ex-Homestyles.

surprises.description: GAAP operating margin fell below even the low end of the 6.5%–7.0% guide, at about 6.0%. Management attributed 70 basis points of the shortfall to an unfavorable foreign-currency translation loss; gross margin was 22.0%, with the currency swing accounting for a 130-basis-point year-over-year impact.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP operating margin was approximately 6.0%, falling below the 6.5%-7.0% guidance due to an $800,000 (70 basis point) unfavorable foreign currency translation loss”; “Gross margin declined to 22.0% from 23.5% a year earlier, driven by a 130 basis point swing in foreign currency.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the “genuine bar is revenue ≥ ~$113M with GAAP operating margin at or above the 7.0% high end,” and flagged a print below 6.5% as a bear outcome.

surprises.description: Freight and diesel-related cost inflation emerged as an additional near-term pressure beyond the tariff costs emphasized in the preview: management cited $1.5–$2 million of incremental inflation in Q1 and expected it to recur in Q2. The company plans a further 2%–3% average price increase to help offset the pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ocean freight rates have nearly doubled over the past six months and diesel-driven inflation is pressuring materials, with incremental inflation of $1.5M-$2M in Q1 and expected to repeat in Q2”; “Management plans an additional average price increase of approximately 2%-3% to help offset rising cost pressures.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed tariff costs and existing pricing of roughly 10%–11%, but did not flag this additional freight- and diesel-driven inflation or a further 2%–3% price increase.

surprises.description: The Q2 sales outlook calls for growth against the difficult $118.2 million prior-year comparison, rather than merely a flat result. The guided range implies approximately 1%–4% growth, which is a modestly better forward signal than the preview’s cautious flat-to-up base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 FY2027 guidance calls for sales of $119.5M-$123.0M (1%-4% growth).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described its base case as “Q2 guided cautiously flat-to-up” and said that guiding Q2 to growth against the $118.2 million comparison “would be a genuine positive surprise.”

surprises.description: Quarter-end cash was much lower than the preview’s hoped-for cash build: Flexsteel reported $4.4 million of cash and slightly negative operating cash flow. The preview did note that Q1 is seasonally the weakest working-capital quarter, which tempers the shortfall versus its cash-build scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $4.4 million in cash, $80.5 million in working capital, and no bank debt, while operating cash flow was slightly negative due to seasonal Q1 outflows.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “a cash build toward $30M+ without revolver draw supports continued repurchase capacity,” while also noting that Q1 is seasonally the weakest working-capital quarter.
